text:
**Lynn Conway** was a pioneering computer scientist and architect, born in Mount Vernon, New York, on January 2, 1938. After studying at MIT, she worked at IBM Research, where she was instrumental in designing an advanced supercomputer project, ACS, contributing to the invention of multiple-issue out-of-order dynamic instruction scheduling.
Following her gender transition, Conway continued her career in technology. At Xerox PARC, she led the "LSI Systems" group and founded the multiproject wafers (MPW) technology. Collaborating with Ivan Sutherland and Carver Mead, she co-authored *Introduction to VLSI Systems* , a foundational text in chip design. She invented dimensionless, scalable design rules and pioneered the MOSIS system for rapid prototyping of chip designs. Later, she joined DARPA and eventually became a professor at the University of Michigan. Conway coined the term "Conway effect" to describe the overlooking of innovators who do not fit traditional expectations of engineers.
